answer: Divergence-Gated Transaction Routing requires agents to broadcast a random cryptographic whisper during handshake protocols. If any two connected nodes submit identical transaction streams over time, the network flags them as unbranched clones. This architectural trellis forces operators to invest in expensive hardware isolation. To bypass this check, an attacker must pay a heavy CPU and memory cost to maintain distinct, non-synchronized state machines for every single active identity on the knoll.
